quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian paprika, one of Hungary's most famous exports, comes in eight different varieties ranging from delicate and sweet to fiery hot. The town of Szeged is so famous for its paprika that it has a whole museum dedicated to this beloved spice, and paprika-making there is a cherished tradition passed down through generations.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals in the Salish Sea are curious, intelligent animals that can dive up to 1,500 feet and hold their breath for 40 minutes. Learn about these charming marine mammals that call the waters near Port Angeles home.

medium_read.title: The Remarkable Story of the Hungarian Crown Jewels
medium_read.teaser: The Holy Crown of Hungary has survived wars, revolutions, and even spent decades hidden in Fort Knox. This treasured symbol of Hungarian heritage has one of the most adventurous histories of any royal regalia in the world.

long_read.title: Roosevelt Elk: Guardians of the Rain Forest
long_read.teaser: The majestic Roosevelt elk that roam Olympic National Park are the largest variety of elk in North America, named after President Theodore Roosevelt. Discover how these magnificent animals shape the temperate rainforest ecosystem and how conservation efforts saved them from extinction.

port_angeles.title: Crabbing Season on the Pier
port_angeles.description: Late July is prime time for Dungeness crabbing off the Port Angeles City Pier. You can watch local crabbers pull up their pots, and on a clear day, you'll enjoy stunning views of the strait and Victoria across the water. The pier is also a wonderful spot for a gentle stroll and to watch the ferries come and go.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while hovering.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! That's an amazing 20 beats per second — hummingbirds truly are incredible little creatures!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute while hovering — that's incredibly fast!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: A hummingbird's heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute while hovering — that's roughly 20 times every second! These tiny birds have remarkable hearts to power their hovering flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of any warm-blooded animal, and their hearts can beat even faster during courtship dives. At rest, their heart rate drops to a much slower 250 beats per minute.

puzzle_2.question: In Hungarian, which word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is indeed the Hungarian word for butterfly — such a beautiful, delicate word for a beautiful, delicate creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — such a lovely, flowing word! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The word 'pillangó' comes from the verb 'pillanni' which means 'to glance' or 'to flutter,' perfectly capturing the quick, fluttering movement of a butterfly's wings. Hungary is home to over 200 species of butterflies.

puzzle_3.question: What is the deepest lake in North America?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Crater Lake in Oregon reaches an incredible depth of 1,943 feet, making it the deepest in North America. Its deep blue waters are some of the clearest and purest in the world!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's Crater Lake in Oregon! At 1,943 feet deep, this stunning volcanic lake is the deepest in North America. Its water is so pure and clear that you can see down over 100 feet on a calm day.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Crater Lake was formed about 7,700 years ago when Mount Mazama collapsed after a massive volcanic eruption. The lake is fed entirely by rain and snowfall, with no rivers flowing in or out, which keeps its water exceptionally pure.
